video_caption: The video opens with a black screen for a second before transitioning to a dark blue background overlaid with faint architectural blueprints. A logo appears, featuring a stylized gold "A" and "E" intertwined with an airplane symbol and a ruler, beside which the text "ARCHITECTS & ENGINEERS for 9/11 TRUTH" is displayed in white. Melancholy orchestral music begins to play. Following this, additional text appears on the screen: "Lynn Margulis" followed by "Docteure scientifique" (Scientific Doctor) at the top, then "Un interview issu du documentaire à venir de AE911Truth" (An interview from the upcoming documentary by AE911Truth) in the middle, and finally, ""Preuves d'explosifs le 11 septembre - Les experts se prononcent"" ("Evidence of explosives on September 11 - Experts speak out") at the bottom, all against the same blueprint background. The scene then cuts to a medium shot of an older woman with short, curly grey hair, wearing a dark blue, shimmering top. She sits at a wooden desk, looking directly at the camera with a calm expression. Behind her is a white Apple iMac displaying a vibrant, complex image of microscopic cellular structures. A white keyboard is visible on the desk in front of her. As she begins to speak, her right hand makes a slight gesture, and French text appears at the bottom of the screen, stating, "Mon nom est Lynn Margulis." (My name is Lynn Margulis.) She continues speaking, explaining her professional background.

In a static, medium shot, an older woman with short, curly gray hair, wearing a dark blue shirt, is seated and speaking directly to the camera. Her facial expressions are animated as she talks, occasionally nodding. To her left, a white Apple iMac computer displays a vibrant, colorful scientific image of a cell, showing a blue nucleus surrounded by intricate green and red filamentous structures. Overlaying the image is text that reads: "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis". In the foreground, part of a keyboard is visible. Throughout the video, French subtitles appear, detailing her achievements: "En 1999, j'ai reçu, parmi plusieurs personnes, une Médaille de Science de William Clinton. Et, il y a deux jours, j'ai reçu le prix Da Vinci. C'est la carte de membre de la Société de Da Vinci. Et je les cite : « La société pour l'étude de la pensée est fière d'annoncer qu'ils me remettent ce prix, Le but de la Société est de développer une banque d'idées de classe mondiale et de promouvoir l'excellence de la pensée en développant un groupe sélect des plus grands penseurs existant dans le monde. » C'est un tant soit peu exagéré, mais ils m'ont remis ce prix." (In 1999, I received, among several people, a William Clinton Science Medal. And, two days ago, I received the Da Vinci award. This is the membership card of the Da Vinci Society. And I quote them: "The society for the study of thought is proud to announce that they are awarding me this prize, The goal of the Society is to develop a world-class thought bank and to promote excellence in thought by developing a select group of the greatest thinkers existing in the world." It's a bit exaggerated, but they awarded me this prize.) The setting appears to be an office or study, with a light-colored wall in the background.

An older woman with short, curly grey hair and a dark blue patterned blouse sits at a wooden desk, speaking directly to the camera with animated hand gestures and a conversational expression. Behind her is a white Apple iMac computer displaying a vibrant scientific image of a cell with blue nuclei and a complex network of orange and green structures, labeled "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis." A white keyboard sits in front of the computer, and various small objects, including a wooden box and pen holders, are on the desk to her right. The background shows a slanted ceiling, indicating an attic or a room with an angled roof. A French subtitle at the bottom translates to: "I reconstruct past natural history from clues considered representative, and that's exactly what we're doing by reconstructing what destroyed these buildings on September 11th using clues that we consider representative. In historical science, that's what one has to do."

A middle-aged woman with short, curly grey hair and a dark purple blouse sits in front of a white Apple iMac computer, speaking directly to the camera. On the computer screen, a vibrant scientific image depicts a cell's cytoskeleton in red and green, with several blue-colored nuclei, and text that reads "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis." The woman uses hand gestures to emphasize her points as she talks, appearing engaged and earnest. French captions are displayed at the bottom of the screen, translating her speech into French: "La science, par-dessus tout, est une façon de savoir, (Science, above all, is a way of knowing,) une façon de savoir à laquelle tous peuvent contribuer (a way of knowing to which everyone can contribute), Cela prend des connaissances, bien sûr, qui continuent d'être développées. (This takes knowledge, of course, that continues to be developed.) Mais ainsi, on peut tout savoir sur tout. (But thus, one can know everything about everything.) Et à la fin de toute activité scientifique, (And at the end of any scientific activity,) on verra qu'on a recueilli des preuves (we will see that evidence has been gathered) qui soutiennent une hypothèse. (that supports a hypothesis.) Et si les preuves contredisent l'hypothèse, (And if the evidence contradicts the hypothesis,) on doit abandonner cette hypothèse et en chercher une autre. (one must abandon this hypothesis and look for another one.) Pour tester une hypothèse ou tenter de l'établir, (To test a hypothesis or try to establish it,) on doit tenir compte de toutes preuves pertinentes, (one must take into account all relevant evidence,) obtenues de diverses façons : (obtained in various ways:) en observant, en mesurant, etc. (by observing, measuring, etc.) Et pour peu qu'on soit vraiment objectif, (And as long as one is truly objective,) on en viendra aux mêmes conclusions. (one will come to the same conclusions.) Fondamentalement, la science est un moyen utile et exact (Fundamentally, science is a useful and exact tool) un outil universel pour comprendre le monde. (a universal tool for understanding the world.)" Behind the computer, various desk items like pens and pencils are visible.

An older woman with short, curly, graying hair, wearing a dark blue/purple top, sits in front of a white Apple iMac computer, speaking directly to the camera and using hand gestures. On the computer screen, a vibrant, colorful microscopic image depicts red, yellow, and green cellular structures, with a blue, circular nucleus-like object, and the text "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis" displayed below it. A white keyboard and mouse are on the desk, along with some pens in a holder and yellow sticky notes on the left side of the computer. French subtitles at the bottom translate to: "So, scientists must always gather information, evidence, what they have observed and measured, to establish the validity of a tested hypothesis. Then, if everything they have observed and measured agrees, if everything is in accordance with the original premise, the conclusion must be published and be openly and clearly accessible for everyone to evaluate. If the hypothesis is indeed correct, its evaluation will stand. This means that a scientist has no better friend than a good critic, a competent critic they can respond to. And if the criticisms led to the abandonment of the hypothesis, because it doesn't hold up, because the facts contradict it, then the hypothesis must be dropped and replaced by something more adequate."

A woman with short, curly grey hair and a dark blue/purple blouse speaks directly to the camera from a desk, using hand gestures. Behind her on the left, an Apple iMac monitor displays a vibrant image of cells: a blue circular nucleus surrounded by intricate red and yellow filamentous structures, identified by text on the screen as "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis." (cytosquelette d'origine spirochète, par hypothèse). To the right of the monitor, a pen holder and other desk items are visible. French subtitles appear throughout her speech, conveying a discussion about science and hypotheses: "Toujours par la science, la formulation exacte de l'idée de base, l'hypothèse, est maintes fois confirmée par bien des gens sous plusieurs aspects, et crée d'habitude de sous-hypothèses ou des à-côtés qu'on peut aussi analyser. Bien sûr, la science n'est jamais secrète quand elle est bien faite. Je dirais qu'il n'est point de mauvaise science. Mais il y a bien de choses qu'on dit science et qui ne le sont pas. Parce que la science est un moyen de découvrir qui s'auto-corrige et qui implique beaucoup de personnes, invariablement, les mêmes constats ou des constats générés par l'hypothèse elle-même. Somme toute, ce sont des règles sur lesquelles les scientifiques du monde sont d'accord." (Always by science, the exact formulation of the basic idea, the hypothesis, is often confirmed by many people from several aspects, and usually creates sub-hypotheses or side aspects that can also be analyzed. Of course, science is never secret when it's well done. I would say there is no bad science. But there are many things that are called science and are not. Because science is a self-correcting way of discovery that involves many people, invariably, the same observations or observations generated by the hypothesis itself. All in all, these are rules on which scientists around the world agree.)

A woman with short, curly grey hair, wearing a dark blue satin blouse, is speaking directly to the camera with an earnest expression, her mouth open as she articulates. Her left hand rests on a white computer keyboard. Behind her to the left is a white Apple iMac computer displaying a vibrant microscopic image of cells: a prominent blue circular cell is centered amidst intricate red and yellow fibrous structures. White text on the screen below the image reads: "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis". To the right of the computer, a cluttered shelf with pens and other objects is visible in the background. A French subtitle appears at the bottom of the screen: "La Science n'est pas science à moins d'être publique, à moins qu'elle soit pleinement ouverte à la critique par quiconque voudrait la critiquer." (Science is not science unless it's public, unless it's fully open to criticism by anyone who would want to criticize it.)

An elderly woman with short, curly grey hair, wearing a dark blue, shiny blouse, is seated at a desk, looking directly at the camera and speaking animatedly. To her left, a white Apple iMac displays a vibrant, colorful scientific image with the text "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis" (cytosquelette d'origine spirochète, par hypothèse). A white keyboard rests in front of the computer. The background is a dark, possibly sloped, wall, suggesting an attic or home office setting, with various office supplies visible. As she speaks, French subtitles appear at the bottom of the screen, starting with "Trois édifices s'écroulent presque en chute libre," (Three buildings collapse almost in freefall,) then "à la vitesse de la gravité." (at the speed of gravity.) followed by "Et pour deux d'entre eux, la cause est l'impact des avions," (And for two of them, the cause is the impact of planes,) and "et pour le troisième, c'est une cause mystère, plutôt," (and for the third, it's a mystery cause, rather,) then "il n'y a pas vraiment d'hypothèse cohérente," (there isn't really a coherent hypothesis,) and "autre que celle qui dit qu'ils sont en feu." (other than the one that says they are on fire.) The subtitles continue with "L'hypothèse la plus évidente pour qui visionne les films - et ils sont nombreux - est que ces édifices se sont effondrés en une démolition contrôlée causée par des explosifs soigneusement placés des semaines, sinon des mois, à l'avance." (The most obvious hypothesis for anyone looking at the films - and there were a lot of people - is that the buildings came down because there was very carefully controlled demolition with high explosives that had been planted many weeks, if not months, in advance.)

An older woman with short, curly, grayish-brown hair, wearing a dark blue, possibly satin, short-sleeved top, sits at a desk and speaks directly to the camera with a serious expression. To her left, a white Apple iMac computer displays a colorful scientific image, likely a micrograph, showing cellular structures in yellow, red, and two prominent blue oval shapes, with text on the screen reading "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis." A white keyboard is positioned in front of the computer. To the right, a pen holder with various writing instruments and some papers are visible, along with other desk items including a silver electronic device. The background suggests an office or study setting, possibly with a sloped ceiling. French subtitles appear throughout the segment, accompanying the woman's speech about the removal of evidence in relation to a "crime" and the rapid destruction of buildings, stating that without material evidence, science cannot reconstruct the facts.

A woman with short, curly, greyish hair, wearing a dark blue top, speaks animatedly, her mouth open and her right hand gesturing. She is seated in what appears to be an attic office, with a sloped ceiling visible behind her. To her left, a white Apple iMac computer displays a vibrant, colorful image on its black screen, showing microscopic structures in bright yellow-orange, red, and blue. Text on the screen reads: "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis". A white keyboard is positioned in front of the computer. French subtitles appear at the bottom of the screen, stating: "surtout si votre hypothèse est la moins valable plutôt que la plus probable," (especially if your hypothesis is the least valid rather than the most probable,).

A woman with short, curly grey hair, wearing a dark purple top, is speaking directly to the camera, gesturing occasionally with her hands. She is seated at a desk with a white Apple iMac computer to her left, displaying a scientific image that appears to be a microscopic view of cellular structures, with the text "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis" visible below the image. A white keyboard is in front of her, and some pens and other desk items are visible to her right. French subtitles appear throughout her speech. At the beginning, the subtitles read: "La prétention du NIST est qu'il n'y a pas de preuves d'explosifs, qu'il est donc inutile d'en chercher." (NIST's claim is that there is no evidence of explosives, so there's no point in looking for them.) She continues: "C'est là la façon la plus non-scientifique qu'on puisse trouver, de ne pas chercher parce qu'on ne s'attend pas à découvrir des preuves. En fait, la preuve est criante que ces cristaux rouge-gris sont des produits d'incendiaires de température extrêmement haute." (That's the most unscientific way you can think of, not to look because you don't expect to find evidence. In fact, there is overwhelming evidence that these red-gray crystals are products of extremely high-temperature incendiaries.) Her speech and the subtitles continue: "Ils ont donc beaucoup de preuves pour quelque chose qu'ils ne peuvent expliquer, ils n'y jettent même pas un coup d'œil, les ignorent complètement, ignorants, et éliminent du coup la thèse d'explosifs. Et, c'est le comble, ils amènent un argument qui est sciemment faux, qu'aucun homme de science n'acceptera, que des feux de bureaux puissent amener l'effondrement d'édifices virtuellement en chute libre. Ils arrivent à ces conclusions à partir de preuves inexistantes et omettent des conclusions basées sur des preuves réelles. Ce ne sont pas là des procédés scientifiques, du tout." (So they have a lot of evidence for something they can't explain, they don't even look at it, they completely ignore it, ignorant, and thus dismiss the explosives thesis. And, to top it all off, they bring an argument that is knowingly false, that no man of science will accept, that office fires can lead to the collapse of buildings virtually in free fall. They arrive at these conclusions from non-existent evidence and omit conclusions based on real evidence. These are not scientific processes, at all.)

A woman with short, curly grey hair and a serious expression, wearing a dark blue blouse, speaks directly to the camera from an indoor setting. To her left, a white Apple iMac computer displays a vibrant, abstract biological image of a cytoskeleton with orange and yellow lines against a dark background, and two prominent blue oval shapes, with the text "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis" visible on the screen. A white keyboard rests in front of the computer. French subtitles appear at the bottom of the screen, starting with "La première règle, généralement, d'une enquête criminelle est de tirer, sur la scène du crime, le plus de preuves possibles de ce qui s'est passé." (The first rule, generally, of a criminal investigation is to collect, at the crime scene, as much evidence as possible of what happened.), then continuing with "Il y avait ces colonnes en acier, en segments tous à peu près égaux, qui furent évacuées, des preuves détruites et éliminées immédiatement après la commission du crime. En plus d'être non-scientifique, c'est illégal." (There were these steel columns, in segments all about equal, which were evacuated, evidence destroyed and eliminated immediately after the commission of the crime. Besides being unscientific, it's illegal.), and finally, as the video ends, "De nombreux témoins, des pompiers et autres, ont rapporté avoir vu du métal fondu qui coulait," (Many witnesses, firefighters and others, reported having seen molten metal flowing,).

In the video segment, a middle-aged woman with short, curly grey hair, wearing a dark blue, silky top, sits facing the camera and speaks with an expressive face and occasional hand gestures. To her left, a white Apple iMac computer displays a vibrant microscopic image on a dark background, showing intricate cellular structures in shades of red, green, and yellow, with prominent blue, oval-shaped elements. Below the image, white text on the screen reads: "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis," indicating the subject of the image. French subtitles are present throughout the segment, translating her English speech. For example, at 00:03, the subtitle reads: "De nombreux témoins, des pompiers et autres, ont rapporté avoir vu du métal fondu qui coulait," (Many witnesses, firefighters and others, reported seeing molten metal flowing,), and later at 00:46, "C'est bien clair que si vous devez mentir en niant ou omettant des preuves, vous n'êtes en rien un scientifique. Ce que vous faites vraiment c'est mentir." (It is clear that if you have to lie by denying or omitting evidence, you are not a scientist at all. What you are really doing is lying.) The background is a simple, light-colored wall.

In the video segment, an older woman with short, curly, grey hair, wearing a dark blue shiny top, is seated at a wooden desk and speaking directly to the camera. Her expression is serious and animated, and she occasionally gestures with her hands. Behind her, an Apple iMac computer displays a scientific image on its screen, which appears to be a magnified view of a cell with a yellow and red filamentous network (likely the cytoskeleton) and two blue oval structures (likely nuclei). Text on the screen reads: "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis". On the desk to her left, a white Apple keyboard and mouse are visible, along with a small yellow sticky note on the computer screen's frame. French subtitles at the bottom of the screen read: "en niant et en omettant des faits cruciaux qui s’opposaient à leurs idées préconçues." (by denying and omitting crucial facts that went against their preconceived ideas.).

The video opens with a medium shot of a woman with short, curly grey hair and a purple top, seated at a wooden desk, speaking directly to the camera. To her left, a white Apple iMac displays a colorful microscopic image of cells, with text "cytoskeleton of spirochete origin, by hypothesis" (English) and French subtitles appearing at the bottom of the screen, saying "Bien voilà, des gens font ça tous les jours et appellent ça de la « Science ». Et ceux qui le font se disent des scientifiques, moi je dis qu'ils ne font pas des science. Ils font de la propagande ou bien de la publicité, qu'importe ce qu'ils font, mais ce n'est pas de la Science. Ça ne respecte pas les règles de la Science." (Well, people do that every day and call it "Science." And those who do it call themselves scientists. I say they don't do science. They do propaganda or publicity, whatever they do, but it's not Science. It doesn't respect the rules of Science.). A white keyboard and mouse are visible on the desk. The scene then transitions to a dark blue background with a faint blueprint overlay, where gold text appears, listing production credits: "Interviewer: Richard Gage", "Vidéographie: Martin McGee", "Postproduction: Charles Ewing Smith", "H.Koch, W.Visser", and "Traduction: C.F.M. & Sandra Jelmi" (Translation: C.F.M. & Sandra Jelmi). The blueprint at the bottom identifies "THE WORLD TRADE CENTER" and "33rd & 34th FLOOR PLAN".
